content.comment_body: Hello, I created a yard sprinkler system using [product_name] and [product_name] screen. The controller operates 6 solenoid valves in sequence, each opening for 10 minutes before the next one starts. An RS relay is controlled by F1 and F2 buttons on the [product_name] device: F1 sets, F2 resets. I want the relay to reset itself after all zone timers complete so manual intervention isn't needed before using the sprinklers again. I'm using On Delay timers for each zone, totaling 6 timers, plus others for extra functions. The program is written using ladder diagram. Thanks for any help.

Personally, I don't enjoy ladder programming. I developed my program in FBD first and then converted it to ladder. Valve times can be adjusted on the display when the sprinkler system is off. While operating, the display shows the remaining time for each valve.

Hi, thank you for the prompt response. I'm the opposite—I don't work much in FBD. I've attached my program for review. My display shows remaining time for each zone, and system pressure through a 4-20 mA analog input from the pressure transmitter, which works well. However, I still want it to reset once all timers finish, which I haven't yet managed. I'll try using a memory bit and keep you updated.
I've applied the same logic using your file, except I made the changes in FBD and then switched it to ladder.

Hi, I followed your earlier example, and everything works perfectly. Thanks! I have more questions. My pressure transmitter is connected, and I'm able to read system pressure on the [product_name] screen, but can't use it to control the pump. Currently, I use an electronic pressure switch that only switches on/off. I’d like to use the pressure transducer to manage the pump via controller relay output to a VFD—say, output Q11 turns on when pressure drops below 3.8 BAR and turns off at 5.8 BAR. How can this be done? Also, is it possible to set the sprinkler duration on the [product_name] screen—sometimes I want each sprinkler to run 15 minutes instead of 10. Is that doable? Thanks again.

Quick update: I succeeded in controlling the VFD output based on the pressure transmitter input. Now, Q11 activates below 3.8 bar and deactivates at 5.8 bar. If you get a chance, please review this setup. The remaining question is about setting times through [product_name] screen.

Sorry, but I don't have the time or motivation to convert your ladder program to FBD, restructure it, make modifications, and convert it back. Perhaps someone else who prefers ladder programming can assist. In my initial example, I have already demonstrated how to modify the starting value of the times on the display.

I encourage you to reconsider your approach. There's a solid reason why our expert uses FBD; I also retrain my students to use FBD for [product_name] rather than the ladder diagram taught in school. Ladder coding for [product_name] has issues and doesn't perform optimally. [company_name] included it mainly to appear competitive with other brands for ladder code on such devices. Refer to the official examples here: [url]. Changing your strategy can be difficult, but it will be beneficial over time.

It wasn't my intention to persuade you to use ladder diagram—it’s just a personal choice. I asked for advice as I thought this was the right place. I’ll figure things out sooner or later. Thanks to everyone for your help!

Sorry for my previous post—it was meant as a helpful warning, not superiority. [product_name] can behave unpredictably with ladder programming: this forum has examples of coded coils not executing. If you prefer ladder, consider other brands like ZEN or ZELIO; my preference is ZELIO. To help, please see the attached file with an idea for your issue as I understood it. The German language forum is very active about [product_name]. You’re welcome to post there in German too (no sarcasm intended).

No offense taken; sorry if my previous answer seemed that way. My use of ladder comes from school training and the equipment I work with, where everything is programmed with STL and ladder. This is my first time working with [product_name], so I wasn't aware of issues with ladder and [product_name], but it's surprising considering [company_name] and German engineering. I just wanted some tips to save time, which I've received—thank you. I speak German but usually prefer using English for forums, though I might try the German forums. I'm transitioning from [product_name] to a KTP 400 Basic panel, so we'll see how that goes. Thanks again for your help.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed challenges automating the reset of the RS relay in a [product_name]-based sprinkler system using ladder diagram, wishing for automatic reset after zone timers finish. The conversation highlighted personal preferences between ladder diagram and FBD programming, noting reliability concerns and differences in support. There was interest in dynamically adjusting timer settings from the [product_name] display, but this remained unresolved. Programming style recommendations and technical workarounds were presented, centering on efficient use of [product_name] devices and clear solutions for pressure-based control.
analysis.user_expectations: The user would like the RS relay to reset automatically when all timers complete to reduce manual input. They hope to set or adjust irrigation durations directly from the [product_name] interface. Additionally, they expect reliable operation and feature equivalence whether using FBD or ladder diagram programming approaches.
